title: Sex-specific phosphate curves do not establish incremental grip-strength prediction: a two-release NHANES test
abstract: In complete-case adults from NHANES2011–2012(source n=4310) and separately sampled2013–2014(target n=4828),adding sex-specific phosphate curves to a shared-phosphate demographic/body-size/chemistry model did not meet the registered incremental-prediction criterion for combined grip strength. Target weighted MSE gain was -0.122553kg²(source-and-target PSU-refit95%interval [-1.509259,+0.977368]);positive favors augmentation. This model-specific negative result is not equivalence,absence of phosphate physiology,or a refutation of published phosphate–inflammation associations. No new physiological signal or clinical utility is established.
